concepts.title: Biodiversity
concepts.definition: The total variety and number of distinct living organisms existing on Earth, currently estimated to be between 1.7 and 1.8 million described species.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Represents the immense range of life forms inhabiting the biosphere.
question_patterns: What is biodiversity and what is its estimated range?
How many species have been described so far on Earth?
Define biodiversity according to taxonomic studies.
What does the term biodiversity refer to?
give one everyday example of biodiversity

solution_steps.explain: Biodiversity refers to the number and types of organisms present on Earth.

solution_steps.action: State the range of described species
solution_steps.explain: The number of known and described species ranges between 1.7 to 1.8 million.
Biodiversity reflects the immense variety of life forms in the biosphere, and the vast majority of species are still undescribed, highlighting the need for continued taxonomic exploration.

concepts.title: Nomenclature and Identification
concepts.definition: Nomenclature is indeed the standardized naming of organisms so they are known by the same name globally, which requires correct description and identification first.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Standardizing names prevents confusion caused by local vernacular names.
question_patterns: Why is there a need for nomenclature of living organisms?
What is the difference between identification and nomenclature?
Explain the role of ICBN and ICZN in naming organisms.
How do biologists ensure that each organism has only one scientific name?
list the main features of nomenclature and identification

solution_steps.explain: Identification is describing an organism correctly to know what name should be attached to it.
Nomenclature is the process of assigning a standardized scientific name to an identified organism.
ICBN (International Code for Botanical Nomenclature) is used for plants, and ICZN (International Code of Zoological Nomenclature) is used for animals.

concepts.title: Binomial Nomenclature
concepts.definition: A standardized naming system introduced by Carolus Linnaeus where each scientific name is made up of two parts: a generic name and a specific epithet.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A two-word format using Latinized terms to uniquely identify species.
question_patterns: What is binomial nomenclature and who proposed it?
State the universal rules of binomial nomenclature.
How is the scientific name of mango written correctly?
Explain the components of a biological name with an example.
give one everyday example of binomial nomenclature

solution_steps.action: Identify the two components of a biological name
solution_steps.explain: The first word is the Genus (capitalized) and the second is the specific epithet (lowercase).
Scientific names are Latinized, written in italics when printed, or separately underlined when handwritten.
The author's abbreviated name appears at the end, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

concepts.title: Taxonomy and Taxa
concepts.definition: Taxonomy is the study of classification of living organisms into different categories called taxa using their characteristics.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Taxa represent categories of classification at different hierarchical levels.
question_patterns: What is taxonomy and what are its basic processes?
Define the term taxon with examples.
Explain how taxa can represent categories at different levels.
What are the essential bases of modern taxonomic studies?
explain taxonomy and taxa in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Taxonomy is the process of classifying organisms into categories based on their characteristics.

solution_steps.action: Identify the four basic processes of taxonomy
solution_steps.explain: Characterisation, identification, classification, and nomenclature are fundamental to taxonomy.
A taxon (plural: taxa) is a scientific term for a classification category, such as Dogs, Mammals, or Plants, which exist at different hierarchical levels.

concepts.title: Systematics
concepts.definition: A branch of biology concerned with the systematic arrangement of organisms, taking into account their evolutionary relationships.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Systematics goes beyond taxonomy by incorporating evolutionary history (phylogeny).
question_patterns: What is systematics and how does it differ from taxonomy?
What does the word systematics originate from?
Which book was published by Linnaeus using a related term?
Why are evolutionary relationships important in systematics?
describe systematics with an example

solution_steps.explain: Derived from the Latin word 'systema', meaning systematic arrangement of organisms.
It includes identification, nomenclature, classification, and evolutionary relationships between organisms.
While taxonomy deals with classification, systematics goes further by incorporating evolutionary history (phylogeny) to understand organism relationships.

concepts.title: Taxonomic Hierarchy
concepts.definition: The systematic arrangement of taxonomic categories in an ascending or descending order, where each step represents a distinct rank or taxon.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Higher groupings share fewer features: climbing from species up to kingdom, the traits any two members still have in common keep dropping.
question_patterns: What is a taxonomic hierarchy?
List the taxonomic categories in ascending order.
What happens to the number of common characteristics as we go higher in the hierarchy?
Why does classification become more complex at higher taxonomic levels?
short note on taxonomic hierarchy

solution_steps.explain: The categories from lowest to highest are Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum (or Division for plants), and Kingdom.
Lower taxa share more common characteristics, while higher categories share fewer common features, making relationships harder to determine.

solution_steps.action: Apply the hierarchy to classify an organism
solution_steps.explain: For example, a human is placed in Species sapiens, Genus Homo, Family Hominidae, Order Primata, Class Mammalia, Phylum Chordata, and Kingdom Animalia.

concepts.title: Species
concepts.definition: The lowest and most basic taxonomic category, consisting of a group of individual organisms sharing fundamental morphological and genetic similarities.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Distinct morphological differences allow one species to be distinguished from other closely related ones.
question_patterns: Define species as a taxonomic category.
Give examples of specific epithets for mango, potato, and lion.
How is a species distinguished from closely related species?
What is the species name of human beings?
give one everyday example of species

solution_steps.explain: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
In Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum, and Panthera leo, the specific epithets are indica, tuberosum, and leo.
Distinct morphological differences allow one species to be distinguished from other closely related species within the same genus.

concepts.title: Genus
concepts.definition: A taxonomic category that comprises a group of closely related species which share more common characteristics with each other than with species of other genera.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: An aggregate of closely related species.
question_patterns: What is a genus in biological classification?
Explain genus with examples of Solanum and Panthera.
How does genus differ from species?
Which genus do potato and brinjal belong to?
state two key points about genus

solution_steps.explain: A genus is an aggregate of closely related species sharing several common features.
The genus Solanum includes potato and brinjal; the genus Panthera includes lion, leopard, and tiger.

solution_steps.action: Explain how genus differs from species
solution_steps.explain: A genus groups multiple closely related species that share more common features with each other than with species of other genera, making it a broader category than species.

concepts.title: Family
concepts.definition: A taxonomic category that groups related genera together, characterized by having fewer similarities compared to the genus and species levels.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Plants are grouped using their vegetative and reproductive traits; animals are grouped on overall body resemblance.
question_patterns: Define family as a taxonomic category.
On what basis are plant families characterized?
Name the family that includes Solanum, Petunia, and Datura.
Distinguish between the families Felidae and Canidae.
short note on family

solution_steps.explain: A family is a group of related genera with fewer similarities than genus and species.
Plant families are characterized based on both vegetative and reproductive features.
Cats (Felis) and leopards (Panthera) are in Felidae, while dogs are in Canidae.

concepts.title: Higher Taxonomic Categories
concepts.definition: Broad taxonomic ranks (Order, Class, Phylum/Division, Kingdom) established by assembling lower categories using shared aggregates of characteristics.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Higher categories represent broader assemblages with fewer shared specific traits.
question_patterns: Explain the higher taxonomic categories with examples.
What is the difference between Phylum and Division?
Which families are included in the order Carnivora?
What is the highest category in biological classification?
how does higher taxonomic categories work

solution_steps.explain: Order is an assemblage of families (e.g., Carnivora includes Felidae and Canidae). Class includes related orders (e.g., Mammalia includes Primata and Carnivora).
Phylum (animals) or Division (plants) groups related classes. Kingdom is the highest category (e.g., Kingdom Animalia and Kingdom Plantae).

solution_steps.action: Explain the trend of shared characteristics at higher levels
solution_steps.explain: As we move up to higher categories, the number of shared specific traits among members decreases, making classification broader and relationships harder to determine.

concepts.title: Taxonomic Classification of Common Organisms
concepts.definition: The specific hierarchical classification of common organisms like Man, Housefly, Mango, and Wheat from genus to phylum/division.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Memorizing and identifying the exact taxonomic categories of key model organisms.
question_patterns: What is the taxonomic classification of housefly?
To which family and order does mango belong?
State the class and phylum of human beings.
Give the complete biological classification of wheat.
list the main features of taxonomic classification of common organisms

solution_steps.explain: Homo sapiens: Genus Homo, Family Hominidae, Order Primata, Class Mammalia, Phylum Chordata.
Musca domestica: Genus Musca, Family Muscidae, Order Diptera, Class Insecta, Phylum Arthropoda.
Mangifera indica: Genus Mangifera, Family Anacardiaceae, Order Sapindales, Class Dicotyledonae, Division Angiospermae.
Triticum aestivum: Genus Triticum, Family Poaceae, Order Poales, Class Monocotyledonae, Division Angiospermae.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Identify the family, order, class, and phylum/division of {organism}.

solution_template.action: Identify the scientific name and genus
solution_template.explain: The housefly is Musca domestica, belonging to the genus Musca.
It belongs to the family Muscidae and order Diptera.
It belongs to class Insecta and phylum Arthropoda.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Determine which of the following is the correctly written scientific name for mango: {name_option_a} or {name_option_b}.

solution_template.action: Check capitalization rules of binomial nomenclature
solution_template.explain: The generic name must start with a capital letter (Mangifera), and the specific epithet must start with a small letter (indica).
Therefore, 'Mangifera indica' is correct, while 'Mangifera Indica' is incorrect because 'Indica' is capitalized.
